  Address/Location: 11711 Hallwood Drive / APN: 8547-001-016

  Request: The Applicant is proposing to demolish an existing 1,719 SF single family home
  and detached garage to allow for the subdivision of an existing 30,638.18 SF lot into three
  (3) individual lots for separate ownership and one (1) common lot. The applicant proposes
  the construction of two (2) 2,481 square foot detached single family residential units, one
  (1) 2,953 square foot detached single family residential unit, three (3) attached garages,
  and one (1) common access lot. The subject property is located in the R-1B (One-family
  Dwelling) zone. This request is being made pursuant to Chapter 16.10 (Subdivisions) and
  Chapter 17.122 (Design Review and Minor Design Review) of the El Monte Municipal
  Code (EMMC).

  CEQA Recommendation: Categorical Exemption – Article 19. Categorical Exemption -

  the California Environmental Quality Act (CEQA) of 1970 and the CEQA Guidelines, as
  amended.

  Case Planner:  Whitney Weisberg, Assistant Planner

  1. Open the public hearing;
  2. Receive presentation from staff;
  3. Pose questions to staff;
  4. Allow members of the public to offer comment;
  5. Pose follow up questions to staff;
  6. Close the public hearing; and
  7. Adopt a Resolution to approve the request and adopt a Categorical Exemption.

  Resolution No.: 3702

  Public Comment:

  A neighbor of the proposed project, Marco Rodriguez (11717 Hallwood Dr), expressed

  possible exposure to asbestos and rodents to the other adjacent properties.

  STAFF REPORT

DATE:  JULY 28, 2026

TO:  PLANNING COMMISSION

FROM:  JERRY MORENO, PUBLIC WORKS & UTILITIES DIRECTOR

BY:  ANA ANANDA, SENIOR PROJECT MANAGER

SUBJECT:  MERCED AVENUE STORMWATER CAPTURE PROJECT,
  CIP-089 – PEDESTRIAN MULTI-USE BIKEWAY TRAIL

APPLICANT:  CITY OF EL MONTE

BACKGROUND

The City of El Monte is pursuing the development of a new linear park (Exhibit 1) for public
recreational use along the existing City-owned El Monte storm drain channel that
discharges to the Rio Hondo Channel. The proposed Merced Avenue Stormwater
Capture Project, CIP-089 (Project) will extend the existing Merced Avenue Linear Park
from Merced Avenue on the east to Brockway Street on the west. The existing storm
drain channel will be converted to an underground box culvert system to create space for
the proposed bike paths and pedestrian walks.

The Project also includes improvements to the El Monte storm drain system, water quality
enhancements, rainwater infiltration systems, and the installation of a shared use path
and pedestrian improvements to connect the Merced Linear Park to the Rio Hondo River
Trail. All construction work will be within the limits of City of El Monte public right-of-way
and planned to be commenced in mid-2027 with the completion scheduled for the end of
2028.

The Project will be funded from the Los Angeles County’s Safe Clean Water Program
(SCWP) (“Project”). The estimated Project cost is $17 million.

  Merced Avenue Stormwater Capture Project CIP-089
  Page 1
 The main goals and objectives of this project are to:
•  Increase recreational opportunities for the local community;
•  Implement new walkable and bikeable paths enhancing connectivity to the 30-mile
  Rio Hondo Bike Path;
•  Bioswale to treat stormwater runoff, reduce reliance on potable water for irrigation and
  mimic natural systems; and
•  Maintain flood control conveyance capacity, provide water quality treatment, and
  provide bikeway connectivity between the Merced Linear Park and the Rio Hondo
  Bikeway.

The City of El Monte initiated the project design to provide access to recreational
opportunities for the local community and to address State water quality requirements
under the current MS4 Storm Water Discharge Permit.

The Project site is approximately 2.56 acres of City property connecting the Merced
Avenue Linear Park (Hero’s Park) to the Rio Hondo Bike Path. Prior to the proposed
improvements, the site housed an open trapezoidal channel that conveys flows from the
Garvey Avenue box culvert to the Rio Hondo Channel.

As part of the Project, a diversion structure will be installed to divert dry weather flows
along with a portion of the wet weather flows, treat those flows in a pre-treatment device
to remove trash, sediment and heavy metals, and then pump them into a bioswale to
further improve the water quality before the flows are returned to the new storm drains
which eventually discharges to the Rio Hondo Channel. This corridor will be between the
backyards of residences on Towneway Drive and Rio Hondo Parkway. Aesthetic steel
screen fences will be installed on both sides of the linear park to enhance the appearance
for park users in addition to ensuring privacy and safety of the residences. Solar lighting,
security cameras, and gates at either side of the project are being incorporated into the
design to further enhance safety and deter unauthorized encampments and promote the
appropriate use of public space.

Extensive and inclusive community engagement has been implemented during the design
phase of the Project and additional engagement is planned. Multiple opportunities were
provided for public participation to inform bike path features and design, including
developing a Public Outreach Plan, social media posts, mailers to the neighborhood
around the channel, posting banners with project information, public outreach events,
community workshops, and door-to-door canvassing. In addition, a Community Advisory
Committee composed of key local stakeholders was established to provide guidance on
site understanding, bike path programming, and review of the evolving concept plan. The
resulting project design reflects the priorities and concerns expressed by residents,
business owners, and community members who will benefit from the conversion of the El
Monte Drain from an inaccessible open trapezoidal channel to an underground box
culvert, bioswale and multi-use path.
